newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus beet harvest slips to 1.00 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Belarus beet harvest slips to 1.00 mln tonnes.

text.p: The Belarus 1996 sugar beet harvest slipped slightly to 1.00 million tonnes from 1.17 million in 1995, Deputy Agriculture Minister Ivan Shokolo told Reuters on Wednesday.
He also reiterated that the government planned to import up to 200,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1997 and said the ministry would hold a tender to choose an importer in the second half of December.
Shokolo said Belarus would produce 100,000 tonnes of refined sugar from this year's harvest, against 140,000 tonnes from the 1995 harvest.
The former Soviet republic had in March targeted a beet harvest of 1.55 million tonnes and said it hoped to cut imports.

Agriculture Minister Vasily Leonov said in October Belarus would produce 120,000 tonnes at its four sugar refineries from its 1996 beet crop, which he then forecast at 1.10 million tonnes. He said Belarus planned to buy 200,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Cuba and Latin America and that a contract had been signed for 120,000 tonnes of South African raws.
Shokolo did not say what stage buying plans had reached.
Belarus requires up to 350,000 tonnes of refined sugar to meet domestic demand.
The government imposed a 35 percent tax on refined sugar imports in October which hit neighbouring Ukraine, traditionally an exporter to Belarus.
